text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Central agency for social security bodies (Acoss) expects 1997 social security deficit to reach 35.2 billion francs, up 4.8 billion francs from the 30.4 billion francs forecast by government. Social security showed a 54.2 billion franc deficit for 1996, 2.7 billion higher than forecasts.
-- State seeks to expropriate nickel miner Eramet from nickel fields in New Caledonia for political reasons linked to independence groups.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis calls for further cuts in labour charges, but is opposed to cuts in value-added tax, raising criticism within the majority.
-- SNPE chairman Jean Faure in an interview says he does not rule out an alliance with Britain's Royal Ordnance.
-- Dexia to buy 40 percent of Italy's Crediop, specialised in financing local administrations.
-- The president of Paris commercial court in an interview says bill project designed to modernise corporate law should have been used as an opportunity for wider reform.
-- Cie de Navigation Mixte subsidiary Via GTI posts a 175.3 million franc loss for 1996 after a 20.5 million franc profit for 1995.
-- White-collar workers to benefit most from the introduction of pension funds in France, study shows.
-- Eurotunnel granted freeze on interest payments to restructure debt.
